subject: Contract: annual term and SLA uplift for Hightower Analytics
messages:
From: Alicia Nguyen <alicia@hightower.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Mejia <c.mejia@hightower.com>, procurement <procurement@hightower.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Renewal windows + SLA ask

Hi Ava,

Hope you’re well — our renewal is coming up for the annual contract that runs Jan 15, 2027. We had a few items the execs asked us to surface ahead of the renewal conversation:

- Can Redwood provide a premium SLA add-on that guarantees 99th percentile p95 and p99 latency targets for text generation (p95 < 250ms for 1k tokens, p99 < 500ms) and a dedicated support path (1-hour response for sev1)?
- We’re expecting a 2.3x increase in Q1 token volume (see attached forecast). How does committed capacity pricing + burst work?
- Any standard language you can provide for a latency SLO in the Statement of Work? Procurement wants proposed wording they can route for legal review.

We’d like to lock terms by mid-November if possible. Carlos is looping procurement.

Thanks,
Alicia Nguyen
Director, Platform Engineering
Hightower Analytics

Attachments: Traffic_Forecast_Q4.xlsx
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Nguyen <alicia@hightower.com>
Cc: Carlos Mejia <c.mejia@hightower.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-02T10:15:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Renewal windows + SLA ask

Hi Alicia — great to hear and thanks for the clarity. High level response and next steps below.

1) Premium SLA & latency SLOs
- We can offer a paid SLA uplift that includes a guaranteed p95 and p99 latency window and a 1-hour response for Sev1 incidents. I attached a short draft SLA addendum (Hightower_SLA_Uplift_v2.pdf) with proposed numeric targets and measurement windows.
- Our SLO language is explicit about measurement method (end-to-end request-to-first-byte on Redwood API across the signed region) and includes an agreed token-length bucket for the latency commitment.

2) Capacity & burst
- For the volume profile you shared, the most cost-effective approach is a Reserved Capacity + Burst pool: a committed baseline for predictable throughput and a modest burst buffer billed at a discounted overage rate. I put a worked example in the addendum based on your forecast.

3) Contract language / timeline
- If you want, Marissa (cc’ed) can prepare a redline-ready one-pager for procurement. We can also provide a short sample SLO paragraph for insertion into your SOW.
- Proposed timeline: finalize scope by 11/12, legal review 11/16, signature by 11/24 to meet Jan 15 start.

Next steps: I’ll follow up with a DocuSign link and consolidated pricing after we confirm the target p95/p99 buckets. Are you available for a 30-minute call tomorrow (11/3) 10:00–10:30am ET to walk the SLA addendum?

Best,
Ava Chen
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Hightower_SLA_Uplift_v2.pdf, Signature_Deck.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Nguyen <alicia@hightower.com>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, procurement <procurement@hightower.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T09:05:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Renewal windows + SLA ask

Alicia — thanks for the call earlier. Key clarifications from our side so procurement has everything in one place:

- SLA targets: we proposed two token buckets (<=1k tokens and 1k–5k tokens). The p95/p99 numbers in the attached are aggressive but attainable with a Dedicated baseline and modest burst headroom.
- Pricing: baseline reserved capacity is quoted as monthly commitment; burst is metered with a cap. We’ll include a monthly cap option to limit unexpected spend.
- Escalation: designated TAM + direct escalation to infra on-call for Sev1. We can add a 2-week onboarding plan to validate latency under your traffic profile.

Ava and I will incorporate procurement redline requests and circulate an updated addendum by EOD 11/04.

-M

From: procurement <procurement@hightower.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Mejia <c.mejia@hightower.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T14:22:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Renewal windows + SLA ask — redlines and questions

Hi Ava / Marissa,

Thanks for the draft. A few redline requests from legal/procurement:

- Measurement & exclusion language: we need blackout windows and scheduled maintenance exclusions spelled out (e.g., planned maintenance windows need 48-hour advance notice and are excluded from SLO calculations).
- Remedies: procurement prefers service credits rather than unilateral termination rights. Can you propose a sliding-credit schedule tied to monthly p99 misses?
- Data residency: confirm that measurement endpoints are taken from the US region only (we need an EU carve-out for now).
- Proof of performance: will Redwood share dashboard access for a rolling 90-day lookback for p95/p99?

Also, our security team asked whether the premium support channel can include weekly incident summaries for the first 60 days after go-live.

Please respond inline; attaching our redline (we converted the pdf text into comments).

Procurement
Hightower Analytics

Attachments: Hightower_SLA_Redline.pdf
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: procurement <procurement@hightower.com>, Alicia Nguyen <alicia@hightower.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T17:42:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Renewal windows + SLA ask — redlines and questions

Hi team — thanks for the detailed redlines. We incorporated the procurement asks into v3 and addressed the specific points below:

- Maintenance & exclusions: added explicit 48-hour planned maintenance notice and a scheduled maintenance SLO carve-out. Emergency maintenance will be limited and communicated; it will only be excluded if documented and agreed after the fact.
- Remedies: we proposed a tiered service credit schedule for monthly p99 misses (1–2% credit for single misses, up to 10% for repeat misses within a 90-day window). Language is in section 4 of the addendum.
- Region measurement: we confirmed US-only measurement for your account by default; EU traffic will be excluded unless you request dual-region measurement.
- Proof & reporting: we will grant read-only dashboard access with a 90-day rolling window and commit to weekly 60-day incident summaries post-go-live.

Next steps: 1) I’ve attached Hightower_SLA_Uplift_v3.pdf with tracked changes. 2) If that looks good, I’ll send a DocuSign envelope with the addendum + order form for the baseline reserved capacity. 3) We’ll provision a 2-week onboarding window starting 1/10/2027 to validate latency under your live traffic.

Action: Please confirm by reply to this thread if the service credit schedule is acceptable and whether procurement wants an explicit monthly cap on burst billing. Once procurement confirms, I’ll send the DocuSign link.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B1234Hightower
